overview: The Medford City Council approved a first reading for a $669,000 loan order to purchase a new fire pumper truck, addressed resident concerns regarding street sweeping and parking citation appeals, and requested draft zoning to enable craft breweries and taprooms.

items.title: Fire Department Loan Order and Operations
items.summary: The Council approved the first reading of a $669,000 loan order for a new fire pumper truck and passed related motions requesting training tower updates, a meeting on fire department capital needs, and a 20-year bond schedule breakdown.

items.title: Street Sweeping, Parking Appeals, and Park Medford Oversight
items.summary: Following resident testimony on street sweeping towing and ticketing, the Council voted to schedule a meeting with Park Medford, request permanent street sweeping signage, and seek reforms to the citation appeals process.

items.title: Brewery and Taproom Zoning Ordinance Request
items.summary: The Council approved a resolution requesting the city solicitor draft a zoning ordinance enabling taprooms, craft breweries, and beer gardens in Medford.

items.title: Municipal Energy Aggregation Presentation Request
items.summary: The Council passed a resolution to reserve time at its February 6 meeting for a public presentation on community outreach and municipal energy aggregation.

items.title: Citywide Pothole Repairs and DPW Resources
items.summary: The Council approved a resolution calling for immediate pothole repairs on major streets and requesting a feasibility study on dedicated DPW repair crews.

items.title: Murray Hill Road Traffic and Safety Measures
items.summary: The Council passed resolutions requesting high-visibility stop sign markings, city boundary signs, and directed police speed enforcement on Murray Hill Road.

items.title: Traffic Commission Schedule, Ashland Street Enforcement, and Commendations
items.summary: The Council requested quarterly evening Traffic Commission meetings and Ashland Street speed monitoring, adopted birthday and condolence resolutions, and approved prior meeting records.
